description: Rows that show money movements, pairing what happened with how much, with read only, action, selectable and expandable variants.

overview.title: Overview
overview.text: A transaction list shows money movements, such as payments, sales, transfers and fees, as rows that pair what happened with how much. Every row has a content block on the left and an amount block on the right. The family shares this structure and adds the behavior each context needs.
whenToUseItems: Lists of receivables, installments and scheduled payments.
Choosing which transactions to pay, advance or export.
Breaking a total down into its parts.
whenNotToUseItems: Rows without an amount: use List.
Settings and navigation menus: use List.
Comparing many columns of data: use a table.
A single balance or total on its own: use a card.

variantRows.readOnly: Shows a transaction that has no action, such as a statement line.
variantRows.action: Opens details or offers actions through a chevron, an overflow menu or a swipe.
variantRows.selectable: Lets people pick one or more transactions with a checkbox or a radio.
variantRows.expandable: Reveals the items that compose a total, such as gross amount and fees.
variantRows.childReadOnly: One item inside an expandable row, on a timeline.
variantRows.childAction: A child item that opens its own details.

formatting.title: Formatting
anatomyRows: What happened, such as "Payment to supplier".
Who it relates to. Emphasized line by default.
Date, order number or due date.
Formatted value; the type adds sign and color.
Status of the transaction, such as Payment scheduled, Processing or Canceled.
One short fact about the amount.
Inset hairline between rows; off on the last row.
formatting.sizesText: Content and amount have two sizes each, set independently with `content.size` and `amount.size`. Use `md` for top-level rows and `sm` for dense lists and child items.
formatting.densityText: `density="compact"` reduces the vertical padding from 16px to 8px. Use it for long lists on large screens; keep the default on touch screens.
formatting.dividersText: Dividers separate rows of the same group. They are inset 16px and on by default; turn them off on the last row so the group edge does not double the container border.

content.title: Content
mainElementsItems: **Title** names the movement in the product vocabulary: "Payment to supplier", "Bank transfer", "Sales received".
**Description** names the counterpart: the supplier, the retailer, the card or the bank. One fact per line.
**Caption** carries the date, the order number or the due date.
**Amount** is always formatted and unsigned (`R$ 6.819,33`); `amount.type` adds the sign and the color.
**Tag** shows the status of the transaction; its type comes from the product's status rules.

default: Values that neither enter nor leave the account.
positive: Money in: sales, Pix received, refunds.
strikethrough: Original value struck, new value in positive color
A discount or a waived fee.
strikethrough-neutral: Original value struck, new value neutral
A changed value that is not a benefit.

content.tagsText: One tag per row shows the status of the transaction. Its type comes from the product's status rules; the examples below follow them. A canceled payment keeps its amount.
doDontItems: Pass the value unsigned and set the type; the negative type adds the sign.
Don't type the sign in the value. The negative type already adds it, so it shows twice.
Show a canceled payment with the neutral Canceled tag and the amount unchanged.
Don't write a sentence in the tag. Keep it to a short status.
Keep the tag short and move the detail to info.
Use the strikethrough types only when the original value really changed, such as a waived fee.
Use `iconColor="on-color"` only on colored backgrounds. On white, its icon is darker than the icons of the rows around it.

behaviors.title: Behaviors
stateRows: Light overlay over the whole row.
Pointer down on an interactive row.
Keyboard focus on an interactive row.
Skeleton in place of the content.
The movement cannot be acted on.
Muted content, neutral tag, no callbacks.
behaviors.interactionText: An Action row is a single target: a click anywhere on it calls `onClick` once. With the overflow menu, the button opens the actions below it on the web; on iOS and Android the same actions open in a bottom sheet. Swipe reveals the actions in place on touch screens.

variants.title: Variants
variants.readOnly: For rows people only read, such as a statement. No hover, no focus stop.
variants.action: For rows that open something. Use the chevron to open details, the overflow menu for two or more actions, and swipe on touch screens.
variants.selectable: For choosing transactions. Checkboxes allow several, radios one. The control sits on the left on the web and on the right in apps.
variants.expandable: For totals made of parts. The row toggles the child items; the supporting text closes the group.
variants.child: Child items sit on a timeline inside an expandable row. Set `position` on each: first, middle, last, or standalone for a single item. Use Child Action when the item opens its own details.

related.title: Related
list: Rows without an amount: settings, navigation and plain content.
tag: The status shown below the amount.
bottomSheet: Holds the row actions on iOS and Android, in place of the web menu.

typography.title: Typography
typography.text: All text uses `font-family-base` ({font}) with `line-height-comfy`. Tokens are listed as md / sm.

size.title: Size
size.text: Row height comes from the content; the values below are the heights with every element shown (title, description, caption, amount, tag and additional data).

provides.title: What Ocean provides
keyboardRows: Moves to the next row, menu button or control. Read only rows are skipped.
Activates the row: opens details, toggles the child items or the menu.
Move between the radios of a group.
Enter / Space on a menu item
Runs the action and closes the menu.
screenReaderRows: Rendered as a native `<button>`; the row text is its name.
Native checkbox or radio; the whole row is its label, so the name includes title, description and amount.
Toggle with `aria-expanded` and a name that says whether it expands or collapses the row.
Named by `menuLabel` (default "Open actions menu"); `aria-expanded` reflects the menu, which has `role="menu"`.
`aria-busy="true"` on the row while the skeleton is shown.
Native `disabled` on buttons and controls; `aria-disabled="true"` on read only rows.
provides.focusText: Interactive rows show a 2px primary outline inside the row on keyboard focus, so the list container never clips it.

considerations.title: Development considerations
items: **Color is never the only signal.** The positive amount and the positive tag text are below 4.5:1 contrast on white. Keep the meaning in the text: the title says what happened and the tag has a label.
**Use Action for anything clickable.** Don’t attach click handlers to Read Only rows; they are not focusable and screen readers don’t announce them as buttons.
**Name the overflow button.** With several rows on screen, set `menuLabel` with the row, such as "Actions for Payment to supplier", so each button has a distinct name.
**Announce new rows.** When more rows load, announce the result in a live region (`aria-live="polite"`), such as "10 more transactions loaded".
**Keep the child order meaningful.** The timeline is visual only; the order of the child items is the reading order.
